title: Back-to-School Isn't Just for Retail Apps
summary: The assumption that "back-to-school" is is reserved for retail apps is wrong, and it's costing non-retail apps a real seasonal opportunity.
body_markdown:
Every year, the same content calendar shows up everywhere: back-to-school sales, backpack discounts, "get ready for the new school year" push notifications. If you're not a retail app, this is usually the point where marketing teams tune out. "Back-to-school is a retail thing. Nothing here for us."


That assumption is wrong, and it's costing non-retail apps a real seasonal window.


This guidance follows the back-to-school timing in the US, Canada, and much of Europe, where the school year usually begins in August or September. In Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, and Brazil, the school year generally begins in January or February.


### What the data actually shows


We pulled OneSignal's own messaging data for apps in the Education category and looked at push notification click-through rates across 2025. From January through May, CTR sat in a fairly steady 0.4% to 0.6% range. **Starting in September, it jumped to roughly 0.9% to 1.2%** , and stayed there through December. That's engagement roughly doubling, and it holds through the whole fall semester, not just the first week of classes.


### The opportunity retail-only thinking misses


Here's the thing about September: it isn't just a shopping event. For EdTech and family apps, it's closer to a **mass re-onboarding event** . Parents are downloading new apps for a kid who just started a new grade. Existing users are returning after a summer of near-total dormancy. Teachers are setting up classes again. Students are logging back into tools they haven't touched since May.


Treating that moment like "just send a seasonal push" undersells it. What actually matters is[onboarding and personalization](https://onesignal.com/the-ultimate-guide-to-user-onboarding-across-channels) built for this specific surge, not a themed one-off message.


A few concrete ways to act on that:


**Segment by role, then tailor the first September message to each audience.** Parents, students, and teachers have different reasons to return, so role-based segments can trigger messages that match their needs instead of relying on recency alone.


**Build a returning-user Journey for people who are reactivating** . Use a return trigger, such as a user opening the app after a period of inactivity, and send a re-engagement message instead of placing that user in a first-time welcome flow.


**Use AI to build it fast, since the window is short** . This surge starts and mostly plays out within a few weeks, not months.[OneSignal AI](https://onesignal.com/ai) can help draft segments and Journey logic in plain language quickly enough to actually catch the window instead of missing it.


### Two other verticals nobody talks about here


EdTech and family apps aren't the only categories with a real, non-retail stake in this window.


**Budgeting** and **fintech apps** have arguably the earliest window of all. Back-to-school spending is projected to hit $43.3 billion this year, averaging $863.86 per family with school-age kids, and 62% of shoppers had already started buying by early July, according to the[National Retail Federation's 2026 survey](https://nrf.com/media-center/press-releases/majority-of-back-to-school-shoppers-get-a-head-start-on-the-season) . Financial planning for the school year begins weeks before retail promotions. A budgeting app can trigger a "back-to-school budget" Journey when a user sets a spending cap, track spending against that cap, and send a reminder as the user approaches it.


**Family organization** and **calendar apps** have a quieter (but real) opportunity too. September is when household schedules reset entirely: new class times, new carpools, new activities, all landing at once. That's a natural reactivation moment for anyone who let a family calendar app go dormant over the summer, and a natural onboarding moment for anyone downloading one for the first time because summer chaos finally became fall chaos.
